transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I can’t sit through long production meetings or edit sessions anymore—I keep getting up and pacing even when I know I should stay in my seat. It's starting to really impact my career because my job has shifted to requiring a lot more of these long, seated sessions lately.
Did these concentration and restlessness problems start in childhood or have they only begun after the recent changes at work or another stressful event?

They actually go back to childhood, though they've become much more of an issue over the last couple of years with my new work responsibilities. Even in elementary school, my teachers would complain to my parents that I couldn't stay in my seat and was constantly getting up to sharpen my pencil or wander around the room.
Besides the restlessness, did you also have trouble with impulsive behavior as a child, like interrupting others, blurting out answers, or acting without thinking?

I don't really recall or have reports of blurting things out or interrupting others when I was a kid. But my teachers constantly complained to my parents that I couldn't stay in my seat and was always getting up to sharpen my pencil or wander the classroom.
Do you also have ongoing problems with attention, like making careless mistakes, losing things, being easily distracted, or having trouble finishing tasks?

Yes, I definitely struggle with that. On tight deadlines, I often make careless mistakes like missing color notes in emails or overlooking typos because I skimmed too quickly. I also find myself drifting off during meetings to think about shot ideas, so I constantly have to ask people to repeat themselves.
Before age 12 and now as an adult, do you also often interrupt people, blurt out answers, or act on impulse without thinking first?

As an adult, I definitely struggle with that—I often blurt out suggestions in meetings before people finish speaking, and I catch myself interrupting colleagues or jumping into conversations uninvited. When I was a kid, though, my issues were much more physical, like my teachers complaining that I couldn't stay in my seat and kept wandering the room.
When you were a child, besides getting out of your seat and wandering, did you also often interrupt others, blurt out answers, or act impulsively without thinking?

I'm not really sure and don't recall if I did those specific things like interrupting or blurting out when I was young. I only clearly remember my teachers constantly complaining about me getting out of my seat and wandering around the classroom.
